encoding_adequacy.question: Does 'CNF UNSAT at T=d(F)' really mean 'no linear circuit with <= d(F) additions computes the factor map'?
encoding_adequacy.soundness_direction: The encoding is an OVER-approximation of circuit existence (it allows schedules where every gate value must lie in {+/- needed targets} = the floor restriction proven by the paper's Lemma). UNSAT of the over-approximation => UNSAT of the true question => no circuit at T. Verified: the CNF has (i) at-most-one-class-per-slot, (ii) every needed class covered, (iii) each gate must be +/- sum of two available (input-or-earlier) values - the exact floor theorem of the paper (gate_b_floor.py module docstring).

control_at_d_plus_1_RAW.setup: Same build_floor_cnf at T=d+1 (floor value set, one idle slot allowed)
control_at_d_plus_1_RAW.interpretation: NOT a broken encoder: at T=d+1 the paper's own witness circuits cannot be represented because each uses ONE aux intermediate whose value class is NOT a needed target (U: u12 = A1 - A4 = (0,1,0,0,-1,0,0,0,0), class outside the 12 needed; V: v9 = v5 + B7, class outside the 13 needed). The floor encoding by construction only allows gate values in the target/input class set - it cannot express ANY witness at d+1, and UNSAT there is the correct answer to the FLOOR question at T=d+1 (which pure-target 14-slot schedules don't exist either).
control_at_d_plus_1_RAW.scan of witness: LEFT_SLP: 13 gates, all 12 needed classes + 1 aux class (u12) created; RIGHT_SLP: 14 gates, 13 needed + 1 aux (v9). Both witnesses are exactly 'floor + 1 aux' - consistent with Mm3's session-2 self-correction (aux-1 at d+1 = possible).

control_at_d_plus_1_AUX1_PASSED.setup: Extended encoding: value set = needed classes + inputs + {the witness's own aux class} at T=d+1 (build_aux_cnf in control_aux1_run.py; fixes a stale-reps bug where classes with no rep inside the floor's base were treated as unreachable even after the base grew).
control_at_d_plus_1_AUX1_PASSED.verdict: Encoder sanity PASS: the aux-1 extended encoder admits the paper's own witnesses at d+1, while the floor encoder correctly reports UNSAT at d (certified) and UNSAT at d+1 (fun but unsurprising: one aux is necessary and the raw floor encoder forbids any aux). The certified UNSAT instances therefore encode precisely the intended floor-impossibility questions.
control_at_d_plus_1_AUX1_PASSED.witness_full_check: The paper's SLPs (LEFT_SLP 13 gates, RIGHT_SLP 14 gates) were walked gate-by-gate: each gate is s1*a+s2*b of previous values, each creates exactly one new class, and all 729 Brent identities for the full scheme were already verified in gate A (campaign 1).

semantics_of_the_certificate: For each factor map F in {U, V, W-factor} of the 55-paper's fixed orientation: no linear circuit over {-1,0,1} with <= d(F) additions computes all targets, where d(U)=12, d(V)=13, d(W-factor)=13. Combined with the gate-A-verified witnesses at d(F)+1 (paper's own circuits), this certifies C(U)=13, C(V)=14, C(W-factor)=14, i.e. the paper's 'provably optimal for this fixed orientation' claim, now with checker-replayed lower bounds.
